 Judgment
The petitioner's land was acquired for the purpose of widening the national highway.

The petitioner approached the District Collector, who is the notified arbitrator under the National Highways Act,19569 (hereinafter referred to as "Act" for short), to adjudicate the dispute regarding the compensation award.
That was not entertained for the reason that the request was submitted after three years.

A Division Bench of this Court, in George P.V. v. National Highways Authority of India [2025 (1) KHC 18] held that applicability of the Limitation Act, 1963 is excluded insofar as the arbitration under the Act, in the light of Section 2(4) of Part I of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

entities.text: George P.V. v. National Highways Authority of India [2025 (1) KHC 18]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The request has been rejected without entertaining the same on account of delay,
therefore, such a request cannot be treated as an award.
Being it a statutory arbitration, the writ petition is also maintainable.

This Court in the above judgment also WA NO.2019 OF 2016 2025:KER:59341 held that if the Arbitrator refuses to entertain an application under Section 3G(5),
the writ petition is maintainable to the limited extent, directing the arbitrator to initiate proceedings under the statutory provisions.
No doubt, the long delay can be considered for the purpose of disallowing any interest claimed on the enhanced compensation.
In the light of the legal position enunciated by this Court in George's case (supra), the impugned order is set aside.
We direct the 2nd respondent - District Collector to reconsider the application and decide in accordance with law, after hearing the parties.
